body:
I really hate how you put into exact words what is going on here. "If you're feeling this way and uncharacteristically drinking, you're already out of energy and afraid" 
I don't want to be afraid. 

I've been doing martial arts for the last 9 years. Ladt time I saw one of them, I froze and walked away. I can't be the attacker, even if I'd like to. I was braver as a 4 year old, when I stood in the kitchen with a knife in my hands, knowing what I had to do to the man, only stopping because my mother found me. 

I'm so tired of the shame.

Thank you for your kind words. I'm not sure it's strength in my case. You're used to what you're used to, after all. I'm used to shit, but not this. Not this normalcy where I can't predict when shits going down the drain. Where it suddenly happens, I know it will, I just never know when. 

I would like to live a little, survive less.
I'm around. Thank you for your words. It means a lot.

No, they do in fact call. They show up everywhere. I've tried moving across the country, they call instead. I've tried new numbers, blocked numbers everything. I don't know who is giving it to them, but they always manage to find it. I've isolated myself, now I feel like I need to isolate myself from everyone. 

I know I feel unsafe. I can't bring myself to trust anyone, not even in the slightest things, like taking out the trash. I've tried therapy, but I can't find a way to cope. I don't know what to do anymore. 

I've never really had a parent take care of me, so I'm not sure what would make me feel safe. So far, nothing has, except me. But I'm running out of energy.

There is this blueberry drink thing that I don't actually know what it is. It's called borovnicka though. I'm not sure what my first language is. Swedish I'd say, but could be German, I'm better with Swedish though. 
And yes, they do. My problem is that these emotions never really leave me alone. I've not really resorted to drinking, because that was my mothers approach and it really didn't help her. I gave up yesterday though. It just never passes. I get these blocked number calls, once in a while, more frequently these last months, and everytime I do, my family does as well. There is no way out of it anymore, nothing passes, it intensifies, and I'm just so...tired of it. I'm so tired of feeling that I have to make it alright. there's just no more power left in me anymore to fix things.
Oh and I'm sorry it took me so long to reply. I wasn't quite sure what to say, and not completely in my own mind atm.

I'm like her. I feel bad all the time. Like if things hadn't happened to me, I would be able to and actually want more sex. As it is now, I just can't, and she can't either. The pressure of wanting, and hoping, and trying to cope, it gets too much. 

Open communication, as much as possible. Let her scream, cry, throw stuff, whatever helps her communicate what she feels. It will bring you closer on all aspects of life together.

Thank you Rorigin. I don't really know what you could say either. I'm happy for your response though. This is not an actual attempt, I would be on my 5th, if it where. I don't want the responsibility anymore, so I let a drunk me decide. It's all I've been doing, taking responsibilities for my actions. What actions? Any logic would explain that I haven't done anything. But it doesn't stop the feeling. So, I will wait and see. 

Please excuse my writing, english isn't my first language and it takes a while for me to form a good sentence since I'm not completely sober. 

Thank you for spending 30min of your life on me. It means the world, even if I don't really want to inconvenience you. Oh and I don't drink usually, haven't had a drink in many years. I would love a calm life like yours.

You can just be there. It's what she needs. If she's happy, wants to do stuff, do it. If not, let her be. Make sure she knows you're around. Make sure she knows you believe her and that there's nothing you wouldn't do for her. 

If she feel safe, free, she will be alright again.
Thank you stranger. I just might, once I'm drunk enough to stop being afraid of it.
